body:
External reviewer findings on published PRs (GitHub Codex in the wyrd instance) are today invisible to the harness: the pipeline stops at the draft PR, and the Act beat's process-delta ledger only receives what a human remembers to register. That severs the outer improvement loop precisely where the highest-value signals originate.

Proposal: a `pdca triage` subcommand (`cli.py`) that:

1. Pulls a PR's review comments/reviews via `gh api` (the `publish.py` gh machinery).
2. Classifies each finding — BUG / CONVENTION / NOISE / TEST-GAP — by keyword heuristics keyed to the instance rubric's class list, with an optional single model pass for the remainder.
3. Routes by class: BUG on a merged PR → tracker issue + carry-forward note; CONVENTION → candidate gate row or rubric line appended to the act log; NOISE → candidate rubric-exclusion entry.
4. Registers every finding via `act.register_signals` with class-keyed signal names (e.g. `codex-pr:option-default-vs-omit`) so `recurrences()` flags a class that reappears *after* its process delta was applied — the ledger becomes the recurrence tracker for external findings.

The wyrd instance will prove the shape as an instance-owned `scripts/triage-pr-findings` first; filing now so the eventual engine home is agreed.
title: pdca triage: ingest external PR review findings into the Act ledger
